sections.h2: Where is Middletown, Delaware, and how fast has it grown?
sections.html:
Middletown is a town in southern New Castle County, incorporated in 1861, at about 66 feet above sea level. Its population rose from 6,161 in 2000 to 18,871 in 2010, an increase of 206.3 percent, and reached 23,192 in the 2020 Census. Recent land annexations drove much of that growth.

Growth of that size shapes what a seller faces. Much of the housing around the old town center is recent subdivision construction, and a large share of buyers are looking at new homes from builders as well as resale houses. Your house competes with both.

The town center itself is older. Middletown's local newspaper, the Middletown Transcript, first printed on January 4, 1868, and population was only 368 in 1850, so the historic blocks are small compared with the surrounding developments.

sections.h2: What roads connect Middletown to Wilmington and Dover?
sections.html:
Middletown sits between two toll roads. The DE 1 toll road runs along the east edge of town with an exit at Odessa for DE 299, and the US 301 toll road lies just west and north with exits for DE 299 and DE 71. DE 71 runs north and south through town on Broad Street, and DE 299 runs east and west on Main Street.

DART First State bus routes serve the town, including Routes 46, 37 and 302. With no passenger rail in town, access to those highways is a selling point to describe accurately. The US 301 corridor is also where national retail and food chains have expanded.

sections.h2: What employers and services are near Middletown?
sections.html:
An Amazon fulfillment center operates in Middletown, and ChristianaCare runs a 24-hour free-standing emergency department that opened in April 2013 at a cost of $34 million. The town operates its own Electric Department and Water/Wastewater Department.

That last point matters at closing. Town utility accounts are set up for home buyers through the settlement attorneys, so no visit to Town Hall is needed, and the town's utility late fee is 6 percent once a bill is seven days past due.

  • Pay the final electric, water, sewer and trash bills before settlement.
  • Ask your attorney to request a tax and utility payoff figure from the town.
  • Keep your account number and online payment PIN handy for the final bill.

The Appoquinimink School District serves Middletown and was formed when Middletown School District 60 and Odessa School District 61 merged on July 1, 1969. Its high schools include Middletown High School, Appoquinimink High School (opened 2008) and Odessa High School (opened 2020).

St. Georges Technical High School lies northeast of town, and private options include St. Anne's Episcopal School and St. Andrew's School. Many sellers find that school boundaries are the first question from family buyers, so confirm which school your address feeds before you list.

sections.h2: What weather should a Middletown seller plan for?
sections.html:
Middletown averages about 41.68 inches of precipitation and 14.5 inches of snow a year, with a mean daily high of 66 degrees and a mean daily low of 45. Records run from 104 degrees in summer to minus 15 in winter.

That range is hard on roofs, gutters and heating systems. A buyer's inspector will look at roof age and attic ventilation, and a dated furnace is a common negotiation point. Photos of recent repairs and service receipts help a seller document the house.

sections.h2: How do Middletown property taxes work?
sections.html:
Middletown bills a town property tax based on New Castle County assessed value, and New Castle County and the school district bill their own taxes separately. The town mails its bills around August 1, and payment must reach the Town Tax Office by September 30 to avoid penalties. A 1.5 percent penalty applies for each month a bill is overdue.

Seniors 65 and older who have lived in town at least a year may apply once for a discount, with the application due before July 1 for that tax year. The discount attaches to the residence, so a new owner must reapply.

New Castle County reassessed property countywide in 2025, the first such reassessment since 1983, so a seller's current assessed value may be very different from what the last owner paid. Check yours on the county's parcel search before you set expectations. The town's tax page lists two different rates in different places, so ask the Tax Office for the current figure.

sections.h2: What rental rules apply if you are selling a Middletown rental?
sections.html:
Middletown requires owners of rental property to register with the town and have the unit inspected at each change of tenant. The first inspection costs $75, one re-inspection is free, and the unit must be vacant and clean. Rental properties must be re-registered every three years from approval, and owners of two or more rental units, along with authorized agents, need a town business license.

The town's Clean Hands Ordinance means past-due bills and fees at the property must be paid before an inspection can be scheduled. Utility service for a tenant requires a passed town inspection and a $300 deposit, and only electric and trash can go in the tenant's name, while water and sewer stay with the owner.

  • A mobile home buyer cannot set up service until the previous owner's taxes are paid in full.
  • Notify the town in writing of changes in rental information.
  • Ask the town about transfer steps, since its procedures do not spell out ownership changes.

sections.h2: What should a Middletown seller gather before asking for offers?
sections.html:
Start with the paperwork that every Delaware sale needs, because gaps here slow a closing more than anything about the house itself. Having these items ready lets a cash buyer or a listing agent move quickly.

  • Your deed and the name of the closing attorney you will use.
  • The most recent town tax bill and the New Castle County assessed value from the parcel search.
  • Final utility readings for electric, water, sewer and trash, which the town bills itself.
  • The Seller's Disclosure of Real Property Condition Report, completed honestly, with radon information if you have any.
  • If the house is a rental, the town registration, the last passed inspection and tenant notices.

If the house came to you through an estate, the disclosure exemption for fiduciary transfers may apply, and your attorney can confirm it. Delaware's disclosure law also notes that a completed form is a good-faith effort and not a warranty, so complete it carefully but do not treat it as a substitute for the buyer's own inspection.

sections.h2: What does a Middletown sale cost and require under Delaware law?
sections.html:
The usual Delaware realty transfer tax is 4 percent, with 2.5 percent state tax and 1.5 percent county or municipal tax, split equally between seller and buyer by statute. The state's first-time homebuyer reduction trims the buyer's share by 0.5 percent of up to $400,000, a maximum of $2,000.

A Delaware-licensed attorney must conduct the settlement, and sellers of homes with one to four units must give the Seller's Disclosure of Real Property Condition Report before an offer. Nonresident individuals pay estimated tax of 6.6 percent of the gain with Form REW EST when the deed is recorded.

A cash sale lets you set a closing date, but these steps apply to any route. We buy as-is and do not quote a price before seeing the property.

faqs.q: When are Middletown property taxes due?
faqs.a: The Town of Middletown mails bills around August 1 and they must reach the Tax Office by September 30 to avoid penalties. A 1.5 percent penalty applies for each month a bill is overdue.

faqs.q: Who sets my assessed value in Middletown?
faqs.a: New Castle County sets assessed value, and the town applies its rate to that figure. The county completed a countywide reassessment in 2025, the first since 1983.

faqs.q: Do I need to inspect a Middletown rental before tenants move out or in?
faqs.a: Yes. The town requires an inspection at each change of tenant, with a $75 first inspection fee and one free re-inspection. Past-due bills at the property must be paid before scheduling.

faqs.q: How do utilities transfer when I sell a Middletown house?
faqs.a: Account setup for the buyer is handled through the settlement attorneys. As the seller, pay your final bills first, because late charges of 6 percent apply once a bill is seven days past due.

faqs.q: Which school district is Middletown in?
faqs.a: The Appoquinimink School District serves Middletown, with Middletown High School, Appoquinimink High School and Odessa High School among its high schools.
